posts.text:
Our history is our power. And as we celebrate that moment on June 19, 1865 in Galveston, we must still wrestle with what freedom means and the reality of our history.

We’re the home of icons like Frederick Douglass and Harriet Tubman –and also one of the birthplaces of redlining. 

We must continue to define what freedom means and demand for a freedom that lets us pass something off to our children besides debt and lets us feel safe in our own community and skin.

Our communities are safer since I took office because we’ve worked in partnership with our entire law enforcement community.

Our law enforcement officers like Top Cop Awardee Richard Krause work tirelessly and sacrifice so much to keep Marylanders safe. 

Partnership brings progress and nothing else ever will.

In this moment of fear for our immigrant communities, we will not stand by while bad actors defraud our neighbors.

Not today. Not tomorrow. Not ever.

When a family on the Shore needs answers, they will get them from a qualified attorney – not from someone preying on fear and profiting off of it.
